iota_lines: 4.1 To see positivity, use the rational positive definite form $\langle x,y\rangle=\mu(x\iota(y))$ on $J_{\mathbb Q}$: [F1] makes its basis $t_w$ orthonormal. Trace symmetry implies $\langle ax,y\rangle=\langle x,\iota(a)y\rangle$. A rational simple left ideal $U_E\subset J_{\mathbb Q}$ exists from its matrix decomposition and is invariant under both $a$ and $\iota(a)$; restriction of this positive form to $U_E$ is nondegenerate. Thus their matrices on $U_E$ are adjoints and have equal trace. It follows that $\chi_E^J(t_{w^{-1}})=\chi_E^J(t_w)$. Step 2.1 now gives $f_Ed_E=\sum_w\chi_E^J(t_w)^2>0$. The strict inequality holds because a nonzero simple character is not identically zero on a split algebra: it takes value one on an appropriate matrix unit. Therefore $f_E>0$. [F1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

iota_lines: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a complex Lie superalgebra. Restriction along $\iota:\mathfrak g\to U(\mathfrak g)$ and extension by the universal property give mutually inverse correspondences between left $\mathfrak g$-supermodules and unital graded left $U(\mathfrak g)$-modules. The correspondences preserve parity-preserving homomorphisms.

1.2 Conversely, restrict a unital graded left $U(\mathfrak g)$-module action along $\iota$. Applying the quotient relation [F2] to $v$ gives $[x,y]v=x(yv)-(-1)^{|x||y|}y(xv)$; grading and bilinearity are inherited from the module action. Thus the restriction is a $\mathfrak g$-supermodule. [given, F2, algebra]

2.1 Starting from a supermodule, the extension in [F3] restricts to the original action by its defining property. Starting from a $U(\mathfrak g)$-module, the extension of its restriction agrees with the original action on every generator $\iota(x)$ and on the unit; these generate the quotient algebra by [F2], so the actions agree on all of $U(\mathfrak g)$. [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

iota_lines: Assume [[def-finite-weyl-lusztig-basic-set-data]], including P2–P8 and P15′. The free abelian group $J=\bigoplus_{w\in W}\mathbb Zt_w$ is an associative algebra under $t_xt_y=\sum_z\gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}}t_z$, with identity $\sum_{d\in\mathcal D}n_dt_d$. It has an anti-involution $\iota(t_w)=t_{w^{-1}}$ and a perfect symmetrizing trace $\mu(t_w)=n_w$ for $w\in\mathcal D$ and zero otherwise, with $\mu(t_xt_y)=\delta_{x,y^{-1}}$.

3.1 The coefficient of $t_y$ in $t_x\sum_dn_dt_d$ is $\sum_dn_d\gamma_{x,d,y^{-1}}=\sum_dn_d\gamma_{y^{-1},x,d}$ by P7. P2 makes it zero unless $y=x$; then P3 and P5 give the unique coefficient $n_d^2=1$. The left identity is proved in the same way, using cyclic symmetry with $\gamma_{x,y^{-1},d}$; the appropriate unique $d$ comes from P3 applied to $x^{-1}$. Step 1.1 proves that $\iota$ reverses products. Since $d=d^{-1}$ by P6, $\mu(t_xt_y)=\sum_d\gamma_{x,y,d}n_d$ is $\delta_{x,y^{-1}}$ by P2, P3 and P5. This symmetric permutation Gram matrix is invertible over $\mathbb Z$, proving every trace assertion. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]
